senses.gloss: स- + आकूत स- + आकूत, adj. 1. intentional, Lass. 83, 2. 2. significant. 3. wanton. Acc. तम्, adv. intentionally, Kathās. 6, 141.
स-आक्षेप + म् स-आक्षेप + म्, adv. revilingly, Pañc. 24, 12.
शक्र- + आसन शक्र- + आसन, n. a throne, Pañc. iii. d. 270.
शाक- + आहार शाक- + आहार, adj. living upon potherbs, Bhartṛ. 2, 79.
स- + कट स- + कट, adj. bad, vile.

शकट शकट, probably for शक् + अत्र,
 I. m., f. टी, and n. A cart, Hit. i. d. 89, M.M. (n.); Pañc. 8, 15 (ता); Rām. 1, 33, 18 (टी); with प्राजापत्य, name of an asterism, Pañc. i. d. 239 (टा).
 II. m.
 1. A cart-load.
 2. A Daitya slain by Kṛṣṇa.
 III. m. or n.
 1. An implement for preparing grain, Man. 5, 117.
 2. A form of marching an army, 7, 187.
 --Comp.

शाकट शाकट, i. e. शकट + अ,
 I. adj. Relating to a cart.
 II. m. A draught ox.
स- + कटुक स- + कटुक, adj. Harsh, MBh. 2, 1551.
स- + कण्टक स- + कण्टक, adj. thorny.
स- + कमल स- + कमल, adj. abounding in lotus-flowers, Kir. 5, 25.
स- + कम्पन स- + कम्पन, adj., f. ना, accompanied by earthquakes, Chr. 36, 23.
स- + कर स- + कर, adj. 1. bearing toll. 2. with rays.
शकार शकार, m. A silly brother-in-law of a king.

शक्कर शक्कर, and शक्वर शक्वर, i. e. शक् + वन् + अ (with र् for न्),
 I. m. A bull.
 II. f. री,
 1. A zone, a girdle.
 2. A woman of impure caste.
स- + करुण स- + करुण, adj. compassionate, Bhāg. P. 1, 13, 12.
स- + कर्मन् स- + कर्मन्, adj. 1. performing any act. 2. following the same business.
स- + कलत्र स- + कलत्र, adj. with his wife, Pañc. 46, 14.
स- + कलह स- + कलह, adj. quarreling, Kir. 5, 13.
स-कल स-कल, adj. f. ला, 1. whole, Vikr. d. 95. 2. all, Pañc. 53, 21; 55, 12.

शकल शकल (a form of शर्कर by [] intermediate *शक्कर, and with ल् for र्, cf. शर्करा),
 I. m. and n. A part, a portion, a piece, Utt. Rāmac. 46, 19; Pañc. iii. d. 193 (194); 262, 25; a potsherd, Man. 6, 28.
 II. n.
 1. Skin.
 2. Bark.
 3. The scales of a fish.
 4. A kind of (black) pigment.
शाकल शाकल, adj. Epithet of a kind of sacrifice, Man. 11, 200; cf. 256.
स- + कवच स- + कवच, adj. clad in armour, mailed.
स- + कातर स- + कातर, adj. cowardly, Nal. 13, 18.

स- + काम स- + काम,
 I. adj. 1. one who has attained his desire, Rām. 3, 52, 52. 2. being in love, Ṛt. 6, 2.
 II. -मम्, adv. 1. with pleasure, Pañc. 44, 9. 2. indeed, Daśak. in Chr. 195, 4 (for aught I care).
स-काल + म् स-काल + म्, adv. Betimes, early in the morning.
स- + कुल स- + कुल, adj. 1. having a family. 2. belonging to a family.
शकुल शकुल, m. A fish (cf. शकलिन्).
स- + कुल्य स- + कुल्य, m. 1. A distant kinsman, Man. 9, 187. 2. A kinsman in general.
स-कृपण स-कृपण, adj. miserable, Śāntiś. 4, 4.
स-कृप + म् स-कृप + म्, adv. compassionately, Śāntiś. 4, 19.
स-कोप स-कोप, adj., f. पा, enraged, Pañc. iii. d. 27.
स-कोप + म् स-कोप + म्, adv. angrily, Pañc. 38, 11.
स-किरीट-कौस्तुभ स-किरीट-कौस्तुभ, adj. with a diadem and the jewel of Viṣṇu, Pañc. 44, 15.
स-क्रिय स-क्रिय, adj. one who observes his religious duties, Lass. 42, 2.
स- + क्रोध स- + क्रोध, adj., f. धा, wrathful, Chr. 57, 28.
स- + क्रोधन स- + क्रोधन, adj. enraged, Rām. 5, 85, 3.
स- + क्षण स- + क्षण, adj. being at leisure, Bhāg. P. 1, 1, 21.
शकृद्द्वार शकृद्द्व्˚, i. e. शकृत्-, n. the anus.
साक्षात्- + धर्म साक्षात्- + धर्म, m. the living law, Man. 2, 12 (cf. 2, 237).
सकृत्-प्रज सकृत्-प्रज, m. a crow.
शाक्य- + भिक्षुक शाक्य- + भिक्षुक, f. की, a Bauddha nun, Daśak. in Chr. 191, 15.
स-कल-इन्दु- + मुख स-कल-इन्दु- + मुख (cf. कला), adj., f. खी, having a face like the full moon, Vikr. d. 28.

शक् शक्, ii. 9, शक्नु, Par., and i. 4, शक्य, Par. Ātm.
 1. To endure, MBh. 3, 11277.
 2. To be able, Rām. 1, 42, 21; with the infin., Man. 7, 6; with the ptcple. in the signification of the infin., अपूर्यां पूरयन्न् इच्छाम्...न शक्नुयात्, He is not able to satisfy the insatiable desire, MBh. 12, 514. []
 3. Impers. pass. To be fit to be done, MBh. 1, 6678.
 4. The pass. transfers its pass. signification to the infin. which it governs, e. g. न शक्यन्ते नियन्तुम्, Man. 2, 96 (They cannot be restrained); Hit. 11, 6, M.M. (नीतिं ग्राहयितुं शक्यन्ते, They are able to be taught good behaviour); with a ptcple. of the pass. of the Caus. instead of the infin., न शक्यते निवर्त्यमाना, Chr. 46, 23 (She cannot be induced to return).
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass.
 I. शक्त.
 1. Powerful, capable, Man. 2, 109.
 2. Able, Vikr. d. 72; with the infin., Man. 9, 10; with the loc. in the sense of an infin., MBh. 3, 2263; Pañc. iv. d. 28.
 3. Clever, Hit. ii. d. 74.
 4. Diligent, attentive, intent.
 5. Speaking civilly (cf. शच्).
 --Comp.
 --Ptcple. of the fut. pass. शक्य.
 1. Easy to be overpowered, Pañc. iii. d. 53.
 2. Practicable, possible, Rām. 3, 53, 27; Chr. 8, 27.
 3. Transfers its pass. signification to the infin. which it governs, e. g. शक्या रक्षितुम्, Man. 9, 10 (They can be guarded).
 4. Superl. शक्यतम, Most possible, Hit. iii. d. 115 (न शक्यतमाः समीहितुम्, Are not at all to be aspired to).
 --Comp.
 अ-, adj. impossible, Hit. i. d. 89, M.M.; Chr. 57, 25. Anomal. desider. शिक्ष, Par. Ātm. To learn, Man. 2, 20. शिक्षित,
 1. Instructed, Pañc. 94, 20.
 2. Learned, Hit. ii. d. 154.
 3. Disciplined.
 4. Trained (as an animal).
 5. Docile.
 6. Modest, diffident.
 7. Skilful, clever, conversant.
 --Caus. of the desider. शिक्षय, To teach, M.M. 2, 69.
 --With the prep. अनु अनु, अनु-शिक्षित, Learned (by imitation), Utt. Rāmac. 63, 2.
 --Caus. of the desider. To instruct, MBh. 1, 5761.
 --With [] अव अव, अवशक्य, Possible, Caurap. 43.
 --With अभि अभि, Caus. of the desider. To instruct, MBh. 1, 8033.
 --With आ आ, desider. To impart, to grant, Chr. 297, 19 = Rigv. i. 112, 19.
 --With उप उप, desider. To learn, MBh. 3, 1790.
 --Cf. Lat. queo (for quecjo), ne-queo (nequinont, for ne-quic + nont), conari; O.N. hagr, dexter, hagna, prodesse.

शक शक,
 1. m. pl. The name of a people, Man. 10, 44.
 2. A particular caste.
 3. An era, especially that of Śālivāhana, commencing seventy-six or seventy-eight years after the Christian.

शाक शाक, partly शक् + अ,
 I. (m. and) n. A potherb, any vegetable, Man. 2, 246; Hit. i. d. 67, M.M.
 II. m.
 1. Power.
 2. One of the seven द्वीपस्.
 3. An era, especially that of Śālivāhana, beginning seventy-six or seventyeight years after the Christian.
 --Comp.
शकच शकच, Rājat. 5, 176 (? perhaps to be corrected to शकज, A man of Śaka, i. e. Scythic extraction, or a proper name).

शकटार शकटार, m.
 1. A bird of prey (a vulture?), Hit. ii. d. 97.
 2. and शकटाल शकटाल, A proper name, Kathās. 4, 104 (ल्).

शकटिका शकटिका, i. e. शकटी + क, f. A small cart.
 --Comp.
शकन् शकन्, see शकृत्.
शकलिन् शकलिन्, i. e. शकल + इन्, m. A fish.

शाकुन शाकुन, i. e. शकुन + अ, adj.
 1. Of or relating to birds. Man. 3, 268.
 2. Portentous.

शकुनि शक् + उनि (see the last),
 I. m.
 1. A bird, Pañc. iii. d. 140.
 2. The Indian kite, Falco cheela.
 3. A surname of the Aśvins, MBh. 1, 723.
 4. A proper name. Indr. 3, 9.
 II. f. नी, A hensparrow.
 --Probably akin to O.N. haukr; Danish, hog; O.H.G. habuh; A.S. hafoe.

शकुन्त शक् + उन्त (or rather शक् + वन्त् + अ, cf. शकुन), m.
 1. A bird, Pañc. i. d. 155.
 2. The Indian vulture.
 3. The blue jay.
शकुन्तक शकुन्त + क, m., f. तिका, A bird, Utt. Rāmac. 29, 4.

शकुन्तला शकुन्त + ला, f. A proper name, Śāk. 3, 5.
 --Comp.
शकुन्ति शकुन्ति (cf. शकुन्त), m. A bird, Utt. Rāmac. 69, 6.

शकृत् शकृत्, and सकृत् सकृत् (for original स्कृत्, from the old form of the vb. कॄ), n., the base of some cases is शकन्, Fæces, excrement, Man. 2, 182.
 --Cf. σκώρ, σκατός, σκέρ-βολος; A.S. scearn; perhaps Lat. stercus and cerda in su-cerda (rather to शृध्?), etc.; and Goth. spai-skuldrs, Spittle.

सकृत् स-कृ + त्, adv.
 1. Once, Vikr. d. 10.
 2. At once, Vedāntas. in Chr. 217, 5.
 3. With, together. Cf. शकृत्.
--Comp.

शक्ति शक् + ति, f.
 1. Strength, Pañc. i. d. 265; with loc., Bhartṛ. 2, 60 (आत्मदमने, in restraining or ruling one's self).
 2. Power. Hit. pr. d. 31, M.M.
 3. The active power of a deity personified as his wife (as गौरि of शिव, etc.), Kathās. 3, 62 (of the god of love); eight particular goddesses, ब्राह्मी, etc. cf. Wilson, Hind. Th. 2. ed. ii. 52, n. ad Mālat. 74, 5.
 4. Signification, Bhāṣāp. 79.
 5. Allaying opposition.
 6. An iron spear or dart, MBh. 5, 5259; a sword, Mālat. 82, 16.
 --Comp.

सक्ति सक्ति, i. e. सञ्ज् + ति, f.
 1. Contact.
 2. Junction, Kir. 5, 46.
 3. Addiction to, attachment.
 --Comp.
शक्तितस् शक्ति + तस्, adv. According to power or ability, Pañc. 161, 24.
ऽशक्तिता -शक्ति + ता, in भोजन-, f. The faculty of enjoying food, Cāṇ. 40 in Berl. Monatsb. 1864, 409.
शक्तिधर शक्ति-धर, m. A name of Skanda, the god of war.

शक्तिमन्त् शक्ति + मन्त्, adj., f. मती,
 1. Powerful, mighty, Pañc. iii. d. 14.
 2. Able, ib. iii. d. 169.
 3. Having gained a fortune or a competence, Man. 10, 98.

सक्तिमन्त् सक्ति + मन्त्, adj., f. मती, Attached.
 --Comp.

शक्तु शक्तु, and सक्तु सक्तु, m. and n., according to some authorities only m. pl. (Pañc. 252, 10, with स्), The flour of barley and other grain first fried and then ground, Hit. 114, 22 (श्).
 --Comp.
सक्तु सक्तु, see शक्तु.
शक्नु शक् + नु (cf. शच्), adj. Speaking civilly.

शक्र शक् + र, m.
 1. Indra, Rām. 3, 54, 8.
 2. A king(?), Rām. 3, 49, 41 (cf. Gorr. n.).
 3. The name of two trees, Pentaptera arjuna and Nerium antidysentericum.
 --Comp.
शक्ल शक् + ल (cf. शच्), adj. Affable.

शक्वन् शक् + वन्,
 I. m. An elephant.
 II. f. वरी, A river. Cf. शक्कर.

शक्वर शक्वर (cf. शक्कर),
 I. m. A bull.
 II. f. री.
 1. A finger-ring.
 2. A zone. Cf. the last.
शक्तु- + शराव सक्तु- + शराव, m. a pot full of flour of barley, Hit. 115, 2.

शाकटीन शाकटीन, i. e. शकट + ईन,
 I. adj. Relating to a cart.
 II. m. A cart-load as a measure of weight or value.
शाकलहोमीय शाकलहोमीय, i. e. शाकल-होम + ईय, adj. Belonging to the शाकलहोम, Man. 11, 256 (cf. the last).
शाकशाकट शाकशाकट, and शाकशाकिन शाकशाकिन (cf. शाक), n. A field of vegetables, a kitchen garden.
शाकिनी शाकिनी, i. e. शाक + इन् + ई, f. A female divinity of an inferior class, Pañc. 241, 1.

शाकुनिक शाकुनिक, i. e. शकुन + इक,
 I. adj. Of or relating to birds.
 II. m. A fowler, Man. 8, 260; Pañc. iii. d. 158.
शाक्त शाक्त, and शाक्त्य शाक्त्य, i. e. शक्ति + अ or य, m. A worshipper of the female principle, Lass. 2. ed. 87, 9.
शाक्तीक शाक्तीक, i. e. शक्ति + ईक, m. A spearman.
शाक्त्य शाक्त्य, see शाक्त.
शाक्य शाक्य, m. Buddha, the founder of the Bauddha faith, Daśak. in Chr. 191, 15.
सकलवर्ण स-क-ल-वर्ण, adj. Endowed with the letters क and ल (viz. कलह), i. e. Quarrelling, Nalod. 2, 14.
सकाकोल स-काकोल, m. One of the hells, Man. 4, 89.

सकाश सकाश, probably स-*काश (vb. काश्), m. Vicinity, presence, Nal. 1, 21; Pañc. 66, 10; acc. and loc. To, Pañc. 23, 1; Chr. 6, 6; Pañc. 55, 19. Abl. From, Pañc. 220, 14.
 --Comp.
सक्तुल सक्तु + ल, adj. Containing flour.
सक्थन् सक्थन्, see the next.

सक्थि सक्थि, probably सञ्ज् + थन्, n.; the base of some cases is सक्थन्,
 1. The thigh.
 2. A bone.
 3. The frame of a cart.

साकम् साकम्, i. e. स-अञ्च् + अ + म् (cf. साचि),
 I. adv. At the same time, together, Chr. 290, 4 = Rigv. i. 64, 4.
 II. prep. With (with instr.), Kāvya Prak. 103, 6.

साकल्य साकल्य, i. e. स-कल (see कला), + य, n.
 1. Totality, Nalod. 3, 19; instr. येन, Completely, Man. 12, 25.
 2. The whole, all.
साकेत साकेत, n. A name of Ayodhya, Ragh. 13, 79.
साकेतक साकेत + क, m. An inhabitant of Sāketa, Śāk. 90, 23 (Prākṛ.).

साक्तुक साक्तुक, i. e. सक्तु + क,
 I. m. Barley.
 II. n. A quantity of fried grain.
साक्षतम् साक्षतम्, i. e. स-अ-क्षत [] (vb. क्षण्), + म्, adv. Uninterruptedly, Lass. 66, 4.

साक्षात् साक्षात्, abl. sing. of स-अक्ष, adv.
 1. In presence, Nal. 24, 13 (in their presence, being present); before, eye to eye, Indr. 2, 16.
 2. From (cf. सकाशात्, s. v. सकाश), Arj. 1, 12.
 3. Manifestly, evidently, visibly, Man. 2, 237; Pañc. 46, 6; Nal. 1, 4 (सक्षाद्-इव मनुः, like an embodied Manu); with one's own eyes, Pañc. 197, 12.
 4. Openly, Mālat. 6, 13.
 5. As, like.
साक्षात्कार साक्षात्-कार, m. Perception, Vedāntas. in Chr. 215, 24; Bhāṣāp. 84.

ऽसाक्षिक साक्षिक, i. e. साक्षिन् + क, a substitute for साक्षिन्, when latter part of comp. adj.; e. g. अ-, adj. Where there was no witness, Man. 8, 109. अग्नि-, adj. Having fire or Agni as witness, Rām. 4, 7, 4.
साक्षिता साक्षिता, i. e. साक्षिन् + ता, f. Testimony, evidence, Man. 8, 80.

साक्षिन् साक्षिन्, i. e. स-अक्ष + इन्,
 I. adj., f. इणी.
 1. Witnessing, having witnessed, Hit. iv. d. 62.
 2. Attesting.
 II. m. A witness, Pañc. iii. d. 93; with gen. and loc., Pāṇ. ii. 3, 39.
 --Comp.
साक्षिमन्त् साक्षिमन्त्, i. e. साक्षिन् + मन्त्, adj., f. मती, Having or requiring witness.

साक्ष्य साक्ष्य, i. e. साक्षिन् + य, n.
 1. Evidence, Man. 8, 82.
 2. Giving evidence, 8, 62; testimony, MBh. 5, 1225.
स-कल-अर्थ-शास्त्र- + सार स-कल-अर्थ-शास्त्र- + सार, adj. containing the essence of precepts about all things, Pañc. pr. d. 3.
